correctness.rationale: For p>=a>=2, the three metric-specific geometric bounds in the parabolic Besicovitch proof extend with q=p/a>=1: nearly parallel large spatial/time centers force geometric time growth and hence a uniform contradiction after O(a) steps; bounded spatial/very large time centers are excluded by convexity; bounded time/large spatial centers use the unchanged Euclidean estimate, with p/a<=p/2. Homogeneity and ball-volume scaling r^{n+a} then give the standard packing and greedy covering argument. For p<a, an explicit rapidly separated sequence produces an infinite Besicovitch family by concavity of u^{p/a}.

originality.rationale: Dobronravov arXiv:2609.15560v1 proves only the standard anisotropy a=2 threshold. Le Donne--Rigot classify existence of some BCP homogeneous metric on graded groups rather than this explicit two-parameter metric family, and Itoh treats the max-type standard parabolic metric. Exact and synonymous searches, plus current SCOPE overlap checks, found no higher-anisotropy phase diagram for d_{p,a}. Residual risk remains from unindexed contemporaneous work.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the anisotropy weight itself as the exact Besicovitch threshold for every a>=2, strengthens the positive side to constants uniform over all p>=a for fixed n,a, and shows complete failure even of weak BCP below the threshold.
